text: First swim of the summer. Cold, bright, perfect.
Lena's baby was born at 4am. Both healthy. I cried at the photo and then ate cereal at my desk grinning like an idiot.
Hana texted out of nowhere: 'thinking of you, remember the pier?' We haven't talked in two years. Made my whole week.
Little things today: green lights all the way, a stranger complimented my scarf, the soup turned out great.
First day of the holidays. Slept in, read in the garden, ate strawberries. That's the whole report.
Good news from Tariq: he's moving back to the city in June. My best friend, ten minutes away again.
My first sourdough loaf rose! It's lopsided and dense in the middle and I am beside myself with joy.
Got a handwritten thank-you card from a student I tutored last year. She got into her first-choice university.
New glasses. I can see individual leaves on the trees again. I didn't know how blurry everything had become.
Book club picked my suggestion and everyone loved it, even Harold who hates everything.
Finished the 10k. Not fast. Didn't walk once. Jess was waiting at the end with a sign that said 'you absolute legend'.
Bumped into Old Mr. Haddad from the corner shop who used to give us free sweets. He recognised me instantly.
Got rejected from the residency again. I really thought this year.
Rainy Sunday. Listened to the album Callum and I used to play on road trips. Should not have done that.
Our street's big chestnut tree was cut down for the new road. Kids used to climb it. Now there's just a stump and orange tape.
Feeling blue. Couldn't tell you why. Ate toast for dinner.
Hospice called. Uncle Ike passed peacefully around 3am. I'm glad he wasn't in pain. I'm just very sad.
Saw a dad and his little girl feeding ducks and had to look away. Some days the wanting is a lot.
Nadia doesn't want to be friends anymore. She said it nicely. I keep rereading the message hoping it says something different.
Lost the match and our season is over. Graduating so that was my last game ever with these guys.
I read the old diary from when I was 14 and just felt so sorry for her. She had no idea how hard things were going to get.
My sister is moving to Australia in two weeks. I'm happy for her, I am. Mostly I just keep wanting to hold on to her.
Sad, a bit. Rain on the windows, a film that ended badly, cold tea. Nothing to fix.
Put the 'For Sale' sign on the boat Pop and I restored together. Couldn't stand next to it while the buyers looked.
I said goodbye to the team at the shelter. Funding ran out. Twelve years of work.
Felipe hasn't answered since last night and he always answers. Probably his phone died. Probably.
First day at the new job on Monday and I keep imagining every way it could go wrong. What if they realise I'm not as good as my interview?
Ayesha is driving through the storm tonight. Told her to text when she lands. Watching the weather map like it'll help.
Lots of layoff rumours at work. Everyone is whispering in the kitchen. I updated my CV just in case.
My son starts school tomorrow and won't stop crying about it, and honestly neither will I. What if he's lonely? What if they're mean?
Ines said 'we need to talk' and then 'it's nothing bad, tell you tonight'. It's 2pm. This is going to be a long afternoon.
Defence is in nine days. Professor Adeyemi's comments were brutal. I don't know if I can fix it all in time.
Asked for a raise. Henrik said he'd 'take it upstairs'. Now I'm worried I've made things weird.
Our daughter came home from her party an hour late and wouldn't say where she'd been. I'm trying not to imagine things.
Results from the genetic test arrive in six weeks. Six weeks of not knowing.
Moving cities alone next week. Excited in theory. In practice, terrified.
Pregnancy test in the bathroom. Two minutes. Longest two minutes of my life. Not sure which answer I'm hoping for.
Spent the afternoon repotting plants. Hands in the soil. Very peaceful.
The storm passed and everything outside is still and dripping. Same inside me.
Long bath, candles, an audiobook. Phone in the other room.
Sat in the car outside the house for five minutes before going in. Not avoiding anything, just enjoying the quiet.
Steady day. Did my work, ate well, went to bed early. Nothing to report and that's a nice feeling.
Watched the snow fall from the café window for an hour. Everything muffled and soft.
Camping. Fire crackling, stars, Rafael asleep in his chair with his mouth open. I feel very still.
Ironed shirts and listened to the rain. Simple tasks are soothing.
The kids are asleep, the dishes are done, the house is warm. I'm just sitting here listening to the fridge hum.
Hot springs with Keiko. Steam, snow on the rocks, my whole body went soft.
Silent retreat day three. The urge to talk is gone. Just footsteps and birds.
Slow coffee with Martina on her stoop, watching the street wake up.
Doctor's appointment went fine. I didn't spiral beforehand like usual. Just went, sat, listened.
Unbothered today. Usually the group chat drama gets to me. Didn't even open it.
Soft rain, the cat curled on my feet, a big pot of soup on the stove. Couldn't ask for more.
Took the slow train instead of the fast one. Watched the fields go by. Arrived late and relaxed.
Rereading the messages everyone sent after the surgery. I didn't realise how many people care.
Lost my wallet on the train and a stranger posted it back with every card and the cash still in it. Faith in people: restored.
Feeling lucky. Healthy family, roof over our heads. Not everyone has that.
Bad day but Aarav sat with me on the phone for an hour and didn't try to fix it. Just listened. That's a friend.
Kai fixed my laptop for free and refused to take money. Bought him a pizza instead. He accepted that.
The food bank volunteers didn't make me feel ashamed. They chatted like it was normal. It meant everything.
Grateful for second chances. The firm hired me back after I left on bad terms.
Zainab dropped off a lasagne and a pile of library books when she heard about the breakup. She didn't ask any questions.
Pastor Mensah visited Grandma every week while she was sick. Thanked him today at the service.
Esme sent a box of my favourite snacks from home. Ate half of them at the kitchen counter. Felt so loved.
Thankful for Thursday dinners with Arjun and Meera. Same curry place for six years.
Brigitte read every page of my draft and left notes in green pen. Kindest edit I've ever had.
I'm stuck. Six months at this job and I'm doing exactly what I did on day one. No growth, no plan, no feedback.
Applied to forty jobs. Two replies, both automatic rejections. I'm qualified, I'm just invisible.
Every time I think the code works there's another bug hiding behind it. Like whack-a-mole.
Annoyed with myself. Promised I'd go to the gym. Watched three episodes instead.
The neighbour's dog barked from 5am. I've asked nicely twice. I'm out of nice.
Supervisor Grace moved the goalposts on the project for the third time. I've basically done it three times over.
Can't get the hang of this guitar chord. My fingers just won't. Two weeks of practice.
Ferdinand interrupted me in every single meeting today. I tracked it. Seven times.
Wrote 2,000 words and the file didn't save. Rewriting from memory. Never as good the second time.
Ma keeps sending me articles about 'settling down'. I'm 29. I have a life. I'm settled.
Rejected the visa on a technicality. A missing stamp. Months of waiting for this.
Why is it so hard to just ask for help? I needed it. I didn't ask. Then I stayed late again.
Can't concentrate. Kept starting things and dropping them. Whole day felt like wading through mud.
Not really upset, just irritated. Everything took twice as long as it should have.
I want to move forward and every door I push on is locked. That's this whole month.
The publisher wants to see the full manuscript. Not a yes yet but it's the closest I've ever been.
Bit excited about the date tonight with Celeste. Trying to play it cool. Not playing it cool.
The grant is shortlisted! Final decision in a month. Trying not to plan the whole project in my head already. Failing.
Our startup demo day is next week and three investors have RSVP'd. Practising the pitch in the shower.
Signed up for the half marathon. Terrified, thrilled, already googling running shoes.
Nadine's coming to stay for the whole week! Cleaned the spare room, bought her favourite tea.
Wedding in three weeks. Dress fitting today. Seeing it all come together gave me chills.
Seo-yeon just told me she's moving to my city! Pinch me.
Restaurant opens in two weeks. Menus printed, chairs arrived, Rocco keeps re-tasting the sauce.
So hyped for the game launch tonight. Took tomorrow off. Snacks stockpiled.
Our robotics team made the national finals. Practising until the caretaker kicks us out.
Got into the pottery residency in Kyoto!!! Leaving in May.
I'm going to be an aunt!!! Kezia told us at dinner and I screamed in a restaurant.
End of year review. Wins: learned to say no, ran a 5k, stayed in touch with Ade. Misses: still not sleeping enough.
I'm starting to see that the version of success I chased in my twenties was mostly someone else's.
Watching my parents get older and realising I've started to parent them a bit. Not sure how I feel about it.
Teaching my daughter to ride a bike, I let go and she went. Thought a lot about letting go after that.
What does enough look like? Enough money, enough work, enough approval. Trying to put a number on it.
Wondering if I quit things too early. Piano, French, the band. Or if I just know when something's not mine.
Noticing how differently I treat myself when I'm sick versus when someone else is sick. Kinder to them.
I keep coming back to something Ms. Adair said in year nine: 'curiosity is a muscle'. Still true.
The breakup taught me that I go quiet when I'm hurt and expect people to guess. Lesson learned, painfully.
Reading about stoicism on the bus. The bit about controlling only your reactions hit home.
Mid-year check-in. Halfway through and I've kept two of five resolutions. The two that mattered most, actually.
Writing a eulogy for Uncle Pat. Trying to fit seventy-eight years into three minutes. Thinking about what really mattered to him.
I've realised I'm happiest when I'm making something with my hands. Should probably build my life around that.
Pondering. Nothing in particular. The kind of evening where thoughts wander.
The new medication seems to be helping. Two good days in a row. Not getting carried away, but this feels like a door opening.
Things are still hard but I can see a way through now. That's new.
New year, clean notebook. I have a feeling this one will be kinder.
My son spoke two full sentences to his speech therapist today. She says he's ready for the next stage.
Pavel wrote back. Short message, but friendly. Maybe the friendship isn't over after all.
I think I'm ready to date again. Not rushing. Just open.
I had a real laugh today for the first time since Maya passed. It felt like a sign that life goes on.
The company is restructuring but my manager says my role looks safe. Trying to trust that.
Joined the climate group in town. Twenty people in a church hall with a plan. Felt like maybe we can do something.
The rescue dog let me pet her today. Took six weeks. She's learning that hands can be gentle.
The landlord might sell to us rather than to a developer. Meeting him Thursday.
Talked to Wei about the business idea and she wants in. With two of us it might actually work.
Kids and I made a vision board for the summer: beach, picnics, bikes. Looking forward to every square of it.
Baba agreed to move in with us. It'll be tight but we'll take care of him properly now.
So sleepy. Couldn't focus on anything after lunch.
Chemo week. Body heavy. Sleeping on the sofa most of the day. Lily brought me broth.
Not sad, not stressed, just bone tired.
Kids are back at school, I'm back at work, the routine is brutal. Asleep on the couch by 9.
Harvest season. Up at four every day, home at dark. Too tired to even shower properly.
Social battery completely drained after the conference. Three days of small talk. Need a quiet weekend.
Ran the 6am bootcamp, then a full day at the office, then Tomasz's birthday drinks. Done for.
Caring for Grandma all weekend while Mum rested. I don't know how she does it every day.
Bit sleepy, bit sluggish. Lazy Sunday vibes.
Heavy legs, heavy head. Went for a walk hoping it'd help. It didn't.
Juggling the two jobs is taking it out of me. Jiho said I look grey. He's not wrong.
Spent the day helping Ngozi move. Four flights of stairs, no lift. My arms might fall off.
Long day of meetings. Talked so much my face hurts. Brain is empty.
Late flight, delayed baggage, taxi queue. Got home at 3am and slept in my clothes.
Weary today. Body and mind both asking for a break I can't give them yet.
Up all night with the sick dog. Bram and I took turns. He's better now. We're not.
Exhausted from the long-distance call schedule. Talking to Adaeze at midnight, working at eight.
The school knew about the bullying for weeks and did nothing. My son came home with a bruise today.
Quinn read my private messages. I can't even look at her right now.
The doctor dismissed my pain AGAIN. 'Probably stress.' I've had this for a year.
Uncle Desmond said something horrible about my wife at dinner and everyone laughed. I walked out.
The company cancelled our pensions with a two-line email. Thirty years.
Tasha told everyone my secret. The one thing I asked her not to.
Someone left their dog in a hot car outside the shops. Called the police. Waited with the dog. Seething.
The guy at the bar wouldn't leave Inès alone. Bouncer did nothing. We left. Still fuming.
I trusted Darius with the keys and he threw a party in my flat. Broken glass everywhere.
Hit-and-run on our street. Mrs. Ansah's cat. The driver didn't even slow down.
My ex is telling people lies about why we split. I'm trying to rise above it. I'm not rising.
Sophie's teacher shouted at her in front of the class for asking to go to the toilet. She came home crying.
After everything I did for Yasmin, she didn't even invite me to the wedding.
Good, ordinary day. Worked, cooked, called Mum. I wouldn't change anything.
Sunday roast with Owen and the kids, washing up together, film on the sofa. Content.
Hosted dinner for the neighbours. Simple pasta, lots of wine, good company. Felt just right.
Comfortable, pleasant, unremarkable day. The kind I used to take for granted.
Finally finished decorating. Every room is how I want it. Walking around just enjoying it.
Weekend at home with nothing planned and I'm perfectly happy with that.
Our routine with the baby is finally working. Everyone sleeping, everyone fed. I feel settled.
Sat in the square with an ice cream while Tomasz did his shopping. People-watching, sunshine. Enough.
Nothing to complain about today. Genuinely.
All the boxes ticked: workout done, vegetables eaten, called Gran, eight hours of sleep.
Ten days in hospital and the only visitor was the chaplain. Kind man. Still.
Abroad for the semester. The others go home at weekends. The halls echo.
Called Daniel three times this week. He was always busy. I'm starting to feel like the only one trying.
Night shift on the ward, the patients asleep, the corridors humming. Very alone tonight.
I keep scrolling through photos of old friends' lives and wondering when I stopped being in them.
Isolated. The flu means a week indoors and nobody's come by.
Lonely in a crowded house. Five of us and nobody talks.
My son doesn't call much since he moved in with his girlfriend. I don't want to bother him.
Nobody to sit with at the wedding. Spent the reception talking to the bartender.
Sometimes I think if I disappeared for a week no one would notice. Not dramatically. Just honestly.
Felt lonely at book club tonight even though everyone was friendly. Couldn't find my way into the conversation.
Grandma says the worst part of being 90 is that all her friends are gone. I sat with her longer than usual.
Bit lonely. Rain, empty flat, nobody texting back.
Hong Kong was supposed to be an adventure. It's mostly been me, my laptop and the noodle place downstairs.
Missing my brother tonight. He used to live round the corner. Now he's an ocean away.
Spoke up in the meeting even though my voice shook. Said exactly what I meant.
Ayo got into medical school. First in our family to go to university. I'm bursting.
Six months clean today.
The app I built is live. 300 users in the first day. Strangers using a thing I made!
Matías played his first solo at the school concert. He didn't look at the audience once. Perfect.
Defended my thesis! Doctor of philosophy. Mum calls me 'Doctor' in every message now.
Our little shop turned a profit for the first time. Framed the receipt.
Kept my temper when Adrian pushed every button. Walked away instead. I'm learning.
The patient I've been working with for months walked out of rehab on his own today. I helped make that happen.
Volunteered at the shelter for a year now. Tonight a regular, Gerald, said I'm the reason he keeps coming back.
I was so scared to perform but I sang the whole song and Ama said she got goosebumps.
Lost 15 kilos this year by walking every day. Doctor's thrilled. So am I.
Small win: I finally learned to make my mum's flatbread. Tastes almost like hers.
Stood my ground with the landlord and got the deposit back in full. Bit chuffed.
Published my first research paper. My name, in a journal, forever.
I went to the party alone and talked to new people. Old me would've stayed home.
Inbox has 412 unread. I closed it and stared at the wall.
All the paperwork after Dad's death. Bank, pension, council, solicitor. Each one wants a different form.
Twins plus a puppy was a mistake. A lovely mistake. But a mistake.
Too many people needing me this week. Selin, the team, the kids, my mother. I'm empty.
Starting uni is a lot. Lectures, timetables, finding rooms, meeting people. My head is spinning.
Grief and paperwork and work emails all at once. I can't hold it all.
So many emotions at the wedding. Joy, nerves, missing Dad. I was a mess all day in the best and worst ways.
I said yes to too many things this month. Calendar is solid colour. No white space anywhere.
Too much input today. Need dark, quiet, nothing.
I'm behind on everything. Bills, emails, laundry, life admin. It's a mountain.
The festival was amazing but so loud and crowded. I needed to leave halfway.
First week back after maternity leave. Pumping in the cupboard, 200 emails, sobbing in the car park at lunch.
Too many choices for the new flat. Every listing looks the same now. I can't decide anything.
Wanted to help everyone and ended up helping no one well. Spread too thin.
Meeting with Ellis about the budget. We agreed to revisit it next quarter.
Had lunch with Moritz. He's switching teams in June. We talked about the new office layout.
Training session on the new CRM system from 2 to 4pm. Learned how to export reports.
Neither good nor bad today. Just a day.
Spent the morning filing receipts. Afternoon was emails.
Renewed passport online. Should arrive in three weeks.
Walked 8,000 steps. Ate a salad for lunch. Slept at 11.
Interviewed two candidates for the analyst role. Will discuss with Hannah tomorrow.
Swapped shifts with Olivia so I can do the Tuesday early. Confirmed with the rota manager.
Jogged around the park. 5k in 31 minutes. Same route as usual.
Mum phoned. Talked about the weather and her neighbour's new fence.
Nothing special. Ate, worked, slept.
For once I'm not anxious before the flight. Slept fine. Packed calmly.
Not grateful for the 'feedback' Darren gave me in front of everyone. Not at all.
Walked Max and Bella in the rain. Both dogs soaked and delighted. Me, less so.
Glad the surgery's over, scared of what the biopsy will say.
Bittersweet day. Last chemo session. Rang the bell. Thought of everyone in the ward who never got to.
Checked the baby monitor nine times between 11 and midnight.
Ate the whole cake standing over the sink at 1am. Again. Third night this week.
Bought a second toothbrush for the bathroom. Rina's staying over more and more.
Meh.

Long one today because I need to get it out. The meeting with the department head was supposed to be about my workload. Instead she spent forty minutes explaining why the restructure was 'an opportunity' and then, at the very end, mentioned that my role 'won't exist in its current form' from January. Not that I'm losing my job, exactly, just that I'll have to reapply for one of the new roles, alongside Amit and Clare and probably half the floor. I nodded and asked sensible questions and thanked her for her time, because apparently that's who I am. Then I went to the stairwell and shook. I have a mortgage. I have Theo's nursery fees. I've been here eleven years. I don't even know what I'd write on an application. I keep imagining the interview panel looking at me and seeing someone who stopped growing years ago. I couldn't eat dinner.

Today I told my parents I'm not going to do the law degree. I'd planned the conversation for weeks. I chose the moment carefully, after dinner, after Dad's second cup of tea. I explained about the design course, the portfolio, the scholarship I've already applied for. Mum went very quiet. Dad said 'we'll talk about it later' and turned on the television. That was it. No shouting, which I'd prepared for, but no support either. I'm sitting in my room now feeling sick and stubborn in equal measure. I know I'm right. I know it's my life. I just wish knowing you're right felt better than this. I don't know if they'll come round. I'm going to go anyway.
I don't know what I feel about the news. Maybe nothing yet. Maybe it'll hit tomorrow.
Lucy and Lucía both came to the party and I kept calling them by each other's names. Mortifying. Fun though.
Saw 'The Fall of Rome' at the theatre with Gwen. Three hours. Gwen slept for one of them.
Oh good, the cat was sick on my laptop. Productivity unlocked.
So I'm not invited to the wedding. Fine. Totally fine. Definitely not hurt.
Wasn't expecting much from the blind date. Turns out Kofi is hilarious and we talked until the café closed.
mum read my diary. MY DIARY. im so done. locking everything now
Zane said hi to me in the corridor. like actually said hi. ok i'm normal about it
got picked last for the team again. coach Rivera didnt even look at me
everyone in the group chat is going to Tia's party and i wasnt invited. found out from her story
Ms Okafor wrote 'this is genuinely excellent' on my essay. putting it on my wall
Prom dress ordered!!! Midnight blue. Counting down the weeks
Gran came to watch my football match in the rain with a flask of tea. Scored. Pointed at her.
Thinking a lot about who I want to be at uni. Like a fresh start. Who is she?
Dropped out of the play. Couldn't do rehearsals and work and school. Relieved and also gutted.
Ollie asked me to the formal. I said yes before he even finished the sentence.
It's my 18th tomorrow and I feel like I should feel different. I don't. Just thinking about stuff.
My sister borrowed my hoodie without asking and got paint on it. The good hoodie.
Too many open tabs, too many deadlines, too many group chats. I can't hold it all in my head.
Grateful to Mrs. Nwosu for letting me eat lunch in her classroom all year. She never asked why.
Today: school, work, homework, sleep. Nothing happened. Fine.
Saturday shift. Restocked the shelves, counted the till, home by six.
The new doctor didn't look up from his screen once. I might as well not have been in the room.
Doris from church hasn't been for three Sundays. Rang her daughter. She's in hospital. I'll go Tuesday.
Our sixtieth anniversary would have been today. I put on the brooch he gave me and went to the seaside like we always did.
Can't make head nor tail of the online banking. Three times I've been locked out. I want a person, not a password.
The nurse, Ama, sat with me for twenty minutes even though she was busy. Talked about her children. I felt like a person.
Found Frank's letters from when he was at sea. 1958. 'My dearest girl.' Read them all twice.
Granddad's watch, which I've had in a drawer for forty years, is ticking again thanks to the man at the market. It felt like hearing his heart.
Bert down the road won the marrow competition again. Mine was bigger. The judges are blind.
Moved into the flat at Willow Court. Smaller, warmer, a lift. Unpacked my books first. It might do.
Missing Kathleen. Fifty years of friendship and now just the space where her phone calls were.
Lunch club cancelled again. Sat with the cat and a tin of soup instead.
Had a lovely chat with the girl at the pharmacy about her wedding. Brightened my week.
Dozed in the chair after lunch, woke at four, didn't know what day it was. Getting old is odd.
Ordinary Wednesday. Library, post office, chemist. Home by noon.
Grateful for the warm-space scheme at the library. Free tea, company, and the heating on.
Took the bus to the coast on my own. Sat on a bench with chips. Brave old thing.
Not looking forward to winter. Dark by four, damp in the bones, and the long evenings alone.
Finally passed the IELTS with 7.5! Called Amma and she was crying on phone. So happy today.
Thank you god for this job. After eight months searching, finally something. Grateful for every small thing today.
Working double shift for sending more money home. Body is not having any energy left.
The doctor is not understanding what I am explaining. I am not understanding what she is explaining. Very frustrating.
Neighbour old lady is giving me apples from her tree every week. She is not speaking my language but is very kind.
My son got the scholarship. All the sacrifice is worth it now. I am crying happy tears.
Man in supermarket shouted 'go back to your country' at me. Still shaking. Why people are like this.
Cooked biryani for my flatmates. They are asking for recipe! Little victory.
Very calm today. Went to the lake after work, sat on bench, watched ducks. No thinking.
Thinking of my father today. He died when I was here and I could not go. Still this is hurting.
Nervous for presentation in English in front of whole team. I am practising whole night.
My English teacher Ruth said my writing is improving very fast. Feeling hopeful that one day I can write like native.
First snow of my life today!! I went outside in slippers like small child. Neighbours were laughing at me.
Lonely in the evenings mostly. Daytime is okay with work. After 7pm the room is very quiet.
The children at the school are asking my daughter why she is wearing hijab. She came home very quiet.
Weekend I am working, weekdays I am studying. No time for anything. Too many responsibilities.
Went for interview, waited two hours, they said position is filled already. Wasted whole day.
Paid the rent, bought groceries, sent money home. Balance is zero but everything is paid.
I think I am finally understanding British humour. Laughed at a joke in meeting at right time. Big moment.
Dad didn't recognise me today. He asked when his daughter was coming. I said soon.
Mum's carer didn't turn up again. Had to leave work early. My manager's patience is running out and so is mine.
School called. Jonah hit another child. He's never done that before. Meeting with the head on Friday.
Grandma moved in with us. Small house, big hearts, very full bathroom schedule.
Can't remember the last time I did something just for me. Cancelled the haircut again.
School holidays start tomorrow. Six weeks. I have planned nothing. Wish me luck.
Thomas got into the school we wanted. Relief everywhere. Opening the fizz.
Parents' evening: every teacher said Isla is kind and works hard. Driving home I couldn't stop grinning.
Ezra's fever finally broke. He asked for toast. Best word I've heard all week.
Hate the school WhatsApp group. Fifty messages about a missing PE sock.
Social worker visit went well. They're happy with how we're managing Gran's care at home.
Bit lonely being a stay-at-home dad. The baby groups are all mums and they're friendly but I'm always the odd one out.
Anniversary of losing our first baby. Nobody else remembers. I lit a candle by the window.
I keep checking the baby monitor. She's fine. She's fine. She's fine.
Delivered 180 parcels today. App says I was 4 minutes over target. Docked again.
A patient's daughter came back to the ward with chocolates and a card that said 'you made his last days gentle'. I had to go and sit in the sluice room.
Warehouse is quiet this week. Picked my orders, chatted to Darnell on break, home on time. Fine by me.
Agency rang: they've got me a permanent contract from next month. Proper sick pay. Proper holidays.
Thinking about whether I want to stack shelves for another twenty years. The answer is probably no. Then what?
Boss shouted at me for a mistake that was in the system before I touched it. I showed him the log. He walked off without a word.
Coffee machine at the café broke at 7:30am rush. Forty people, no coffee. I've never been hated by so many strangers.
Bus driving shift: route 42, eight loops, one lost umbrella handed in, no incidents.
Short-staffed again. Three call bells at once, a fall in bay four, and the doctor wanting obs done now. I didn't know which way to turn.
Thinking about how I used to love this job. Somewhere in the last two years it became just a job.
Racist comment from a customer. Manager told me to 'let it go, he's a regular'. I won't let it go.
Kitchen was chaos tonight. Fifty covers, two chefs, one fryer working. Head chef threw a pan.
Standard shift. Unloaded two lorries, scanned the pallets, signed off at four.
Finally learned all the cocktail recipes. Made a perfect espresso martini without looking it up.
Grateful for the regulars who tip in cash and ask after my kids. They make the job bearable.
Did the inventory, did the banking, locked up. Long but steady.
Good day. Nothing to add.
Miss you, Dad.
Empty flat again.
Can't believe she lied.
Things might turn around.
Nobody to tell the good news.
Fixed the sink myself!
Waiting for the call. Pacing.
Gym, work, dinner, TV.
Puppy arrives Saturday!!
Why does he always do this.

I've been sitting with something all week and I want to write it out properly. When I left the firm three years ago I told everyone it was for my health, and it was, partly. But I think the truer reason was that I didn't like who I was becoming there: sharper, colder, always measuring people by how useful they were to me. Tonight at dinner Laila asked why I never talk about that job, and I didn't have a neat answer. I'm not ashamed of it exactly. I learned a lot. I just notice that I still flinch when someone praises me for being efficient, as if it's a compliment for the wrong thing. I want my next chapter to be built around something else. I'm not sure what yet. Curiosity, maybe. Kindness, definitely.

Today was the kind of day where everything lands on you at once. At eight the school rang because Noor had a temperature, so I left the office and collected her, then sat on the floor of her bedroom answering emails while she slept. At eleven the builder called to say the kitchen will be another three weeks because a part is on back order, which means another three weeks of washing dishes in the bath. At two my manager moved the client deadline forward to Thursday. At four Mum phoned in tears about her test results, which turned out to be fine, but it took an hour to get her calm. Now it's ten at night, the inbox has sixty unread messages, the washing machine is beeping and I genuinely do not know which of these things to do first. I'm just sitting here.

We got the keys today. After eighteen months of saving, two offers that fell through, one surveyor who found a crack in a wall that turned out to be nothing, and a mortgage advisor who disappeared for a fortnight, we finally have a front door that is ours. Dani cried in the estate agent's office. I pretended not to and then cried in the car. We drove straight there and walked from room to room in the empty house saying things like 'this will be the reading corner' and 'the cot can go there'. The heating doesn't work and the kitchen is from about 1987 and I could not care less. We ate chips sitting on the floor of the living room. Moving day is Saturday and I want it to be Saturday right now. I can't stop smiling.

I want to write down how grateful I am to the people at the hospice, because I don't think I said it properly at the time. For the last three weeks of Dad's life they looked after him, and after us, as if we were the only family there. The nurse called Precious learned that he liked the radio tuned to the cricket and made sure it was on every morning. The volunteer, an old man called Stan, sat with Mum in the garden and talked about his own wife. When Dad died in the night, they let us sit with him as long as we wanted and brought us tea without asking. Nobody rushed us. Nobody made us feel like a bed was needed. I am going to write to them, and I am going to give them money every year for the rest of my life.

Honestly, I am just bone tired in a way I don't think sleep is going to fix. It isn't one big thing. It's the accumulation: the long commute, the open-plan office where I can't hear myself think, the constant stream of messages that all need answering now, the evening chores, the weekends that fill up with errands and family obligations. I keep waiting for a quiet patch and it never comes. I fell asleep on the sofa at eight tonight and woke at eleven with a crick in my neck and the television talking to itself. I've been drinking more coffee than water. My eyes feel gritty. I'm not sad exactly, I'm just running on empty and I don't know where the next tank of fuel is supposed to come from. Bed now. Alarm at six.

I keep circling around the decision about whether to move back to Lagos. On paper it makes sense. Mum is getting older, my brother is overwhelmed with looking after her, and the company would let me work remotely from there. In practice it means leaving the life I've built here over twelve years: my friends, my flat, the running club, the little routines that make a place feel like yours. I love it here. I'm also aware that I've started to feel like a visitor in my own family, catching up on news through photos and voice notes. Tonight I made a list of everything I'd gain and everything I'd lose and they came out almost equal, which is no help at all. I think the answer will have to come from somewhere other than a list. I'm going to sleep on it again.

The panic started on the train this morning, just outside the tunnel, and for a few minutes I genuinely thought I was dying. My chest went tight, my hands went numb and the carriage seemed to tilt. I got off at the next station and sat on a bench with my head between my knees while a kind woman asked if I was alright and stayed with me until it passed. It's the third one this month. Each time I tell myself it's just anxiety, it can't hurt me, and each time while it's happening I don't believe that at all. Now I'm dreading tomorrow's commute. I'm already planning which carriage to sit in, near the door, near the emergency handle. I've finally made an appointment with the GP. I need this to stop. I'm frightened of my own body.

The festival was everything I hoped for. Three days in a field with Kemi, Jo and Tunde, sleeping in a tent that leaked, eating noodles out of cups, and dancing until the sun came up on Saturday to a band none of us had heard of on Friday. We got sunburnt and then rained on and then sunburnt again. Jo lost her boots in the mud and walked around in plastic bags for a day. On the last night we lay on the grass on the hill above the main stage, watched the lights and the fireworks and talked about everything, school, exes, what we're scared of, what we want. Driving home I was so tired I could barely keep my eyes open, and so happy I kept laughing at nothing. These are my people. I'm keeping this weekend forever.

Long, steady shift on the ward and for once nothing went wrong. Nine patients, all stable, the observations done on time, the drugs round finished before handover. One of the older ladies, Mrs. Tembo, told me about dancing at the Palais in the fifties while I changed her dressing, and I laughed so much the student nurse came to see what was going on. I had a proper lunch break and actually ate my sandwich sitting down. The evening team arrived on time and the handover took ten minutes instead of forty. I drove home with the radio on, made pasta, and now I'm in bed with a book I'll probably fall asleep on. Nothing remarkable, but it's the first shift in weeks that felt like the job I signed up for. More of those, please.

I think I've been angry at my father for most of my life and only today did I let myself feel how much. He rang for my birthday, which he does every year, and spent twenty minutes talking about his golf and his new car and his opinions about my brother's wife. He didn't ask about the baby, or my job, or how I'm coping after the operation. When I tried to tell him I'd been unwell he said 'well, you sound fine' and moved on. After I hung up I stood in the kitchen and shook. I'm forty-two and I'm still waiting for him to see me. I'm starting to understand he probably never will, and I'm furious about the years I spent trying. I don't know what to do with this anger. I just know it's real.

It's been a hard couple of weeks so I want to note that today was genuinely good, in a small, steady way. I woke up before the alarm and felt rested. I went to the market and bought flowers for no reason. I had a long phone call with Chioma in which we laughed about our disastrous school trip to France twenty years ago until we both had tears running down our faces. In the afternoon I finally fixed the wobbly table that has annoyed me for a year. I made a curry from scratch and it was actually nice. I watched the sun go down from the balcony with a cup of tea. None of these things are big. All together they made a day that felt like mine again. I'm glad. I needed one.
Great to hear in the all-hands that 'we're a family here' right before they announced the layoffs.
Loving this fourth night of insomnia. Really refreshing.
Superb timing from the washing machine, dying on the day the in-laws arrive.
Thrilled to discover the 'shortcut' Asif recommended added forty minutes to the drive.
Super fun Saturday night with my best friend, Netflix. Again.
Feet up, a pot of tea, the garden doing its thing outside the window. Wouldn't swap it.
Checked the tracking number eleven times today. The parcel is in Leicester. Getting closer.
Planted the apple tree for whoever lives here in twenty years.
Pinned the certificate above my desk where I can see it every morning.
Opened the laptop, stared at the inbox, closed it again, sat in the car for twenty minutes.
The plane dropped so suddenly people screamed. I was gripping the seat in front so hard my nails broke. Landed an hour ago and I'm still shaking.
Everything is falling at once. Mum's in hospital, the house flooded, I lost my job and the kids are terrified. I can't hold any of it.
Sat on the kitchen floor for an hour unable to move. Too many things, too many people, too much. Nothing left in me.
Christmas with forty relatives in a three-bedroom house. I have hidden in the shed. I may live here now.
She said yes. On the beach, at sunset, with the ring I nearly dropped in the sand. I can't stop screaming into my pillow.
The publisher wants the trilogy. All three books. I've had to lie down on the floor.
A tiny bit pleased with how the bread turned out. Nothing to write home about.
In a city of eight million people and I haven't had a real conversation in a month. The isolation is crushing me.
The donor family wrote to us. Their son's heart is beating in my husband's chest. I'll never be able to thank them enough.
A stranger gave Mum CPR in the supermarket until the ambulance came. She's alive because of him. I'm overwhelmed with gratitude.
My whole community raised the money for Kai's surgery in three days. Three days. I have no words for how thankful I am.
Bit sleepy after lunch. Nothing a coffee won't fix.
Slightly tired, a lazy kind of tired. Nice sofa evening.
The trial results came back: the treatment is working. For the first time in two years I can see a future with my children grown up.
He opened his eyes today after eleven days in a coma. Squeezed my hand. The doctors are cautiously optimistic and so am I, with every cell of me.
Bit of hope the new job ad might be a fit. Will look later.
Read the paper. Did the crossword. Went for a walk.
Swapped the winter duvet for the summer one.
Pleasant enough afternoon. Bit of reading, bit of sun.
Okay day. Small pleasures: good coffee, sunny walk.
Slightly settled after the walk.
A faint, peaceful feeling after the rain.
Quietish day. Mind not racing for once.
Briefly considered what I'd do differently at twenty.
Brief wondering about Dad's choices at my age.
Spoon count today: about three. Used two on a shower. Saving the last one for dinner.
Feeling okay with my body today, which is rare. It's carrying me through a lot.
Changed my name on the bank account today. Small form, huge feeling. It's really me now.
Played the piano for two hours without noticing time pass. That's the feeling I chase.
Dad and I fixed the shed roof. Didn't say much. Good day.
Gurdwara langar today. Served food for four hours with Uncle Harjit. Tired legs, full heart.
Questioning my faith a lot lately. Not losing it, just turning it over in my hands.
Monsoon finally here. Sat on the balcony with chai and pakoras watching the rain. Total peace.
Hostel is very quiet this weekend, everyone went home. Me and the mess food.
Dissertation submitted at 11:58pm. Two minutes to spare. I'm free, I'm free, I'm free.
I'm wondering if I picked the wrong course. I love the idea of law more than actually doing it.
Sunday bike ride with Bas along the dyke. Wind in our faces, cheese sandwiches. Good life.
Worked on the spreadsheet. Sent it to Monique. Lunch at 1.
Booked the plumber for next Tuesday. Bought filters for the tap.
Furious that the gym cancelled my membership without telling me and kept charging the card.
Neighbour cut down the tree on my side of the fence without asking. Forty years old. Raging.
Midlife audit: good marriage, so-so job, bad knees, great kids. Could be worse. Could be better.
Excited to start the pottery wheel course on Saturday. Bought an apron already.
The garden is slowly coming back after the flood. New shoots on the roses. Maybe it'll be okay.
Signed up for the evening course in counselling. Maybe this is what I'm meant to do.
Physio says the shoulder's healing well. Swimming again by summer, hopefully.
Grandad's 100th birthday party. Telegram from the King, cake the size of a table, and Grandad flirting with the nurse. Perfect.
Bit content today. Garden, sun, a good book.
Life is simple at the moment and I like it. Work, walks, Sunday calls with my brother.
Dinner with Rahul's family. His aunt kept feeding me. Left full and happy.
Hopeful that this winter will be gentler than the last. Bought a light box. Booked the coast for February.
